title: Lesson 7: Team Delivery: When It's More Than One Consultant, How the Work Splits
description: Recognizing when one consultant stops being enough and splitting work on two axes, with the seam between owners made a written, durable contract rather than a memory.

questions.question: Per the lesson about team delivery, what is the central focus?
options: Splitting work across owners on the axes of who owns it and in what order, with the seam as a written durable contract
A review of unrelated project tools
questions.explanation: The lesson teaches that splitting work is interface design, and nearly every team that fails is failing at a seam, not a part.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects the lesson's guidance?
options: The seam can live in one person's memory because the team is small
Parallel subagents spawned and collected are a durable team
A seam carries what the piece delivers, what it needs, and its acceptance bar, written and durable so both sides can read it
Give every piece a dependency so nothing runs out of order
questions.explanation: The lesson teaches that the seam must be a written, durable thing that both sides can read, because memory lives in one head and dies with the conversation.

questions.question: Which conclusion does the lesson support?
options: A maker can grade their own work because they know it best
A review noted in a status column is as good as a gate that blocks the flow
An anonymous spawned child holds a role across a delivery as well as a named profile
The orchestrator decomposes, routes, and observes, and does not execute the pieces themselves
questions.explanation: The lesson teaches that the orchestrator's deliverable is the shape of the team and the integrity of its seams, not any single piece of production work.
